page: Amazon Web Services c6g.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features the custom AWS Graviton2 processor built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused allocation of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate processing capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test shows average performance at 6053.66, and the single-core test registers at 1519.79. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate average throughput, reaching 71.99 GB/sec for read operations and 35.14 GB/sec for write operations. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in memory-intensive and specialized tasks. Passmark CPU encryption tests score in the lower percentile at 543.57, and the overall Passmark memory score is 1022.79. Additionally, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds are relatively low, reflecting architectural limitations in legacy single-threaded execution and complex instruction sets.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6g.xlarge leverages the ARM64 architecture to deliver a high density of dedicated physical cores relative to its resource footprint. This makes it a viable option for workloads that benefit from dedicated core execution without requiring high memory-to-CPU ratios. Suitable workloads include distributed compute tasks, static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight containerized microservices that do not depend on x86-specific instruction sets.
